failure_definition: Electrode gel degradation causing signal quality degradation
causal_mechanism: Electrode gel degradation in Ag/AgCl electrodes with hydrogel increases electrode-skin impedance, directly degrading ECG signal quality (sensor drift)
current_device_behavior: The ECG monitor currently does not have a mechanism to detect and adapt to electrode gel degradation, allowing signal quality to degrade over time
failure_point: The sensor drift occurs due to the electrode-skin impedance increase, which affects the ECG signal quality
blocking_constraint: The need for a low-power, real-time monitoring circuit that can trigger an adaptive signal quality gating algorithm without significantly increasing the device's power consumption or complexity
